text:
elaine: heads-up — i'm starting a short probe to shrink the console telemetry row shape. goal is to remove per-route jsonb blobs and move small attrs into a compact columnar table. will sketch plan and ask for blockers
pranav: 👍 can you call out the query patterns this affects? dashboards, p99 queries, exports?
derek: most dashboard endpoints hit the wide table for fast UI reads. removing blobs will break a handful of ad-hoc queries but helps our storage and p99 compaction. main risk is backfill time + index bloat during copy.
elaine: good call. affected patterns: per-route p50/p95 p99 (console UI), quota rollup job, billing exports, and one internal ad-hoc: route_label_aggregation.
lina: do we have an estimate for backfill IO and time? last similar compactify took ~14 hours on prod when we did metrics rollup.
elaine: rough calc: ~1.2TB scanned, with copy-through dualwrite we can do ~80 MB/s sustained -> ~4 hours. but need to validate during quiet window and protect OLTP.
pranav: we should dualwrite for a week and run read-adapter that falls back to wide table if missing keys. feature-flag the new read path so UI can switch.
derek: agree. propose steps:
1) add compact table schema + migration that creates indexes (no backfill)
2) start dualwrite from ingest -> both tables behind a flag
3) run backfill in small timeboxed batches (partitioned by tenant)
4) flip read-adapter for canary tenants -> validate queries and perf
5) cutover and drop blobs after safety window

lina: suggestion: use tenant-windowing to limit blast radius. pick 10 low-traffic tenants for canary, then ramp. also add an opt-out for high-sensitivity tenants.
elaine: +1. i'll add canary list. question: how do we avoid index bloat during backfill? if we create indexes before backfill we get bloat, after backfill we risk long reindex.
pranav: create indexes concurrently (postgres: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) after bulk insert per partition. or insert into an unindexed table and swap via partition attach. both have tradeoffs.
derek: for safety i'd prefer partitioned attach trick: write to new partitioned tables, attach to main once partition is ready. reduces lock window.
elaine: will prototype attach method. another risk: dashboard queries expect route attributes in one row; read-adapter needs to stitch. sketch of read-adapter logic:
```
-- pseudo
select coalesce(c.attr_a, w.attr_a) as attr_a
from compact c
full join wide w using (route_id)
where route_id in (...) limit 100
```
We should push some of this stitching into materialized views per-tenant for perf.

lina: also add telemetry to track percentage of reads served from compact table vs fallback. add a console metric and an alert if fallback > 5% for 30m.
pranav: agree. add an observability card in console: per-route hit/miss + p99 latency delta.
elaine: permissions question: compact table will be read by billing-export service. need ACL + audit log. ops: ensure KMS and column redaction config consistent.
derek: noted — i'll add DB view with limited columns for billing exports and a GRANT to billing role.
elaine: deployment plan (proposal):
- dev: schema + adapter behind ff
- staging: dualwrite + small backfill for sample tenants
- prod-canary: pick 10 tenants, run dualwrite + backfill + enable read-adapter for those tenants
- prod-ramp: increase tenants, monitor fallback metric and p99s -> if good, enable global read-adapter -> schedule final blob drop 7 days later

pranav: can we automate rollback? if read-adapter shows >5% fallback or p99 regress, auto-disable adapter and continue dualwrite.
lina: yes, we'll wire a short circuit in the adapter and a deploy-bot hook to flip ff.
deploy-bot: build/infra check passed for schema-change migration id=2026-compactify-01. staging job queued. :rocket:
elaine: thanks. action items:
- elaine: create PR with schema and read-adapter stub
- derek: design partition attach backfill script + ACL views
- pranav: observability cards + FF rollout plan + canary tenant list
- lina: run perf estimate and schedule quiet window ops

pranav: timeline proposal: start staging tomorrow, canary next Thurs, ramp over 2 weeks.
derek: tagging infra to monitor IO during backfill window. cc @infra-team
elaine: will post an update in #eng-platform-announce before staging. ping if any blocking concerns.
pranav: can we also add a small smoke test for the export pipeline so billing exports are validated after backfill?
derek: yes — export smoke test + checksum comparison between wide and compact for sample tenants.
elaine: perfect. i'll open tracked tasks. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
